safari: Skipped: this sample was made on a Mac without Xcode 27.1, so the iPhone Duo simulator wasn't available. The audit stands on its own.

sideways:figure-app-shot.fix: The app preview has a fixed `width: 420px`. Make it `width: 100%; max-width: 640px`, so it fits the closed screen and stays capped on wide ones.

background.fix: `body` is `#111` behind a light page, so Safari would paint a dark column beside it on the closed screen. Give `html` and `body` the page's own colour, `var(--paper)`.

bars:closed-landscape.fix: Make the cookie notice a floating card capped at 520px. On screens under 420px tall, let it join the page instead of floating. The other option is keeping the full-width bar at one line tall.

covered:closed-landscape.fix: Cleared by the cookie-notice change: on the short screen it no longer floats over the hero.

covered:open-landscape.fix: Cleared by the cookie-notice change: a 520px card at the bottom no longer reaches the download buttons.

crease:a-lone:start-writing-free.question: "Start writing, free" is centred alone, so on the open screen it sits on the crease. Add a second button, such as "Take the tour", so the gap between them lands on the crease? Or keep one button and move it to the left on wide screens?
crease:a-lone:start-writing-free.fix: A pair of equal buttons is the smaller change and reads better at every width, but it adds a call to action. That's a content decision, so it's yours.

grid:div-grid.fix: 1 column, then 2 from 600px. Three cards in two columns leave one alone, so the third card spans both columns. The other option is adding a fourth card, which would be a content change.

vh:hero.fix: `min-height: 100vh` sets the hero's height on Open, tall, where Safari's 100vh is 35px taller than what's visible. Add `min-height: 100svh` after it, keeping 100vh as the fallback.

hover:menu-hover-sub.fix: Open "More" on tap: `:focus-within` and an `.is-open` class toggled on click, closing on Escape. Keep hover only inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.

insets:wrap.fix: Set each side from its own inset: `padding-left: max(20px, env(safe-area-inset-left))` and the same for the right.

top-inset:header.fix: Remove `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` from the header. The page doesn't draw under the status bar, and in-app browsers would turn this into a dead strip.

resize.fix: The width is read once at load, so the app preview's sidebar stays hidden after the device opens. Replace the script with a media query: hide the sidebar under 600px in CSS.

ua.fix: Same script: it hides the nav for any user agent that says "iPhone", including the 951px open screen. Collapse the nav with a width media query instead.

screen.fix: Same script: it hides the downloads when `screen.width` is under 600px, and on the simulator that stays at the closed value after opening. Hide them with a width media query instead.

crease-moving:a:ferro.question: With reduced motion on, the customer logos stop with Ferro on the crease. Leave it, or show reduced-motion visitors a static grid of logos?
crease-moving:a:ferro.fix: For everyone else the logos stream past the crease, which Apple allows. A static grid for reduced motion is a small change, but it's a different look for those visitors.

crease-h:button-feedback:feedback.fix: Move the Feedback tab from halfway down to 70% down (`top: 70%`), so it clears the fold on Open, tall. The other option is a round button in the bottom-right corner. The fold's height on this pose is estimated, so check it in Safari.

cover.fix: Drop `viewport-fit=cover`. The page doesn't draw under system UI and uses no safe-area insets, so it gains nothing from it.

cutoff:div-release-strip.fix: A deliberate bleed: the release chips run off the right edge to say there's more. They're labels, not controls, and nothing scrolls.

overlay:div-grain.fix: A film-grain texture over the page at 7% opacity. It ignores taps (`pointer-events: none`) and has nothing to close.
